subject: Intermittent large-upload failures over ClearStone IPsec tunnel
messages:
From: Alex Meyer <alex.meyer@clearstonehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ClearStone NOC <noc@clearstonehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:14:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent large-upload failures to your private instance

Hi Karthik,

We're seeing intermittent failures when our users upload files > ~8MB to the ClearStone-facing app backed by your private deployment. The client usually gets an HTTP 413 or a socket reset; retries sometimes succeed after a few seconds. This started after the last maintenance window on Tuesday (we didn't change app code).

Attached: clearstone-upload-fail-eth-trace.pcap and an example error screenshot (error_screenshot-413.png). The NOC trace shows a few thousand connections per hour that fail briefly and then recover. Our edge team suspects something on the IPsec tunnel between our edge and your VPC is dropping or blackholing larger packets.

Key details from our side:
- Edge: Cisco ASA 5556-X, IPsec NAT-T enabled, ipsec mtu set to 1500 (default)
- Tunnel uses ESP (AES-GCM) with NAT traversal between our public IP and your endpoint
- We see MSS advertised as 1460 in the TCP handshake

Can you confirm whether your ingress/egress devices are dropping ICMP Fragmentation Needed messages or whether there are security group rules blocking ICMP? This looks like a PMTU/DF-bit interaction but we need your team's confirmation.

This impacts end-users; we can provide packet captures and give a maintenance window if you need to apply a quick mitigation.

Thanks,
Alex Meyer
Network Engineer
ClearStone Health
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Alex Meyer <alex.meyer@clearstonehealth.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent large-upload failures to your private instance

Alex, thanks for the quick heads-up and the pcap. I'm looping in Vanessa to prioritize this. High-level asks while we triage:

- Can you confirm whether your ASA is performing MSS clamping on outbound SYNs for tunneled traffic? If not, can you temporarily set MSS to 1300 on the ClearStone-to-Redwood tunnel as a test?
- Please paste the ipsec config snippet for the tunnel (especially NAT-T, DF handling, and any mtu settings).
- If you can, run a quick tcpdump showing the initial SYN/SYN-ACK for a failing upload and include the DF bit on the packets (I saw the pcap but need the DF details clearly labeled).

On our side, we'll:
- Check that our firewall and load balancer allow ICMP type 3/code 4 (fragmentation needed) through to the return path. If those are blocked, PMTU will fail and TCP will hang for large segments.
- Verify our NAT rules and any security group egress filters — sometimes stateful appliances drop ICMP which kills PMTU.

Temporary workaround ideas: chunked uploads or forcing client to use smaller segments; MSS clamp is faster. We'll treat this as an escalation until resolved.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Network & Private Deployments Lead
Redwood Inference
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Alex Meyer <alex.meyer@clearstonehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 17:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent large-upload failures to your private instance

Karthik / Alex,

I'm opening an ops escalation (NETOPS-7891) and tagging SRE on-call. My initial read: this smells like PMTU blackholing across an IPsec tunnel. Common pattern: DF bit set on client -> ESP/NAT-T adds ~50-80 bytes overhead -> intermediate MTU smaller -> router returns ICMP type 3 code 4 (fragmentation needed) but firewall or ACL in the path drops ICMP -> sender keeps DF set -> large packets are silently dropped.

Short-term mitigation to validate the hypothesis:
- Apply MSS clamp 1300 on ClearStone's ASA for traffic destined to our subnet (quick test, no app change).
- Alternatively reduce ipsec MTU on your side to 1400 to account for ESP+NAT overhead.

Longer-term fixes: ensure ICMP frag-needed is permitted across the path and add explicit MSS clamping on the tunnel endpoints. If you need, we can schedule a 30-min window tonight to test.

Laura - can you pull firewall rules for the ClearStone peer (ingress egress) and verify ICMP type 3 code 4 is allowed back to their IP? Also check any load balancer proxy that might swallow ICMP.

-Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Network Success
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Meyer <alex.meyer@clearstonehealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent large-upload failures to your private instance

Vanessa/Karthik, attached is the more targeted pcap (clearstone-upload-fail-eth-trace.pcap) and an ipsec config excerpt (ipsec-config-snippet.txt).

Snippets from our edge:
- crypto ipsec df-bit clear
- nat-t keepalive 10
- ip mtu 1500 on outside interface

From the pcap: the client's SYN has DF=1 and MSS=1460. After the SYN, there are a few retransmits and then the server (your side) sends packets that never seem to reach the client. I also see several ICMP Destination Unreachable (Fragmentation needed) from an intermediate hop but the subsequent path behavior is inconsistent.

If MSS-clamp 1300 is the recommended immediate test, we can apply it during a maintenance window later today. We'll coordinate the change with our NOC.

Regards,
Alex
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Alex Meyer <alex.meyer@clearstonehealth.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 10:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent large-upload failures to your private instance

Alex, thanks for the config and pcap. Quick analysis summary (from the capture and our edge traces):

- I see TCP segments with DF=1 and MSS advertised ~1460.
- There are ICMP type 3 code 4 messages indicating 'fragmentation needed' originating from a transit hop (not from your ASA or our LB).
- The ICMP frag-needed messages are sporadic and some appear to be filtered on the return path (we can see them in the clearstone pcap but not consistently in our egress logs).

Diagnosis: classic PMTU failure across an ESP/NAT-T tunnel where NAT/ESP overhead reduces the effective MTU and ICMP frag-needed isn't reliably delivered back to the sender. That causes large segments to be dropped.

Immediate remediation plan (ordered):
1) TEMP: Ask ClearStone to apply an MSS clamp of 1300 on their ASA for traffic bound to our subnets. This is the quickest test and low risk.
2) TEMP: If MSS change is not possible, reduce IPsec MTU on the ClearStone ASA to 1400 (accounts for ESP+NAT overhead).
3) PERM: Audit firewall/ACLs on both sides to ensure ICMP type 3/code 4 is allowed end-to-end. If policy prohibits raw ICMP, implement tunnel-level MSS clamp permanently.
4) APP: Offer a client-side chunked-upload fallback for large files as an app-level mitigation until the network change is confirmed.

Rollback/validation:
- After MSS clamp, run an upload job for a 20MB file from a representative client while capturing traffic. Expect to see successful large segments and no repeated frag-needed.
- If failures persist, we'll coordinate a 30-min packet-level session with your NOC and our SRE to step through live captures.

I'll hold off on any config changes on our side until you apply the MSS clamp so we can isolate the effect. Please propose a 30-min window tonight (21:30-22:00 PDT) or tomorrow morning.

-karthik
From: Alex Meyer <alex.meyer@clearstonehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ClearStone NOC <noc@clearstonehealth.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent large-upload failures to your private instance

Karthik/Vanessa, quick update: we applied MSS clamp 1300 on the ASA for traffic to your subnets during the 21:30 maintenance window. Post-change: we ran the 20MB test upload 10x and all completed successfully with no 413/connection resets. Monitoring in the wild (12 hours) looks good — failed uploads dropped to near zero.

Action items:
- We want to schedule a joint post-mortem to harden the tunnel: either permit ICMP frag-needed across the path or make MSS clamp a persistent configuration.
- We'll open a change ticket to set ipsec mtu to 1400 if further tests show edge cases.

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Please close NETOPS-7891 when you've captured our final validation logs.

Appreciate the help,
Alex
Network Engineer
ClearStone Health
